stories.label: Bank of England Unanimously Hikes Rates, Warns of 4.9% Inflation
stories.summary: The decision the earlier ECB/BoE preview anticipated: the Bank of England raised Bank Rate a quarter point to 4%, its first hike since 2023, and warned inflation is heading for almost 5% next year as the Iran war's energy shock feeds through. Lead with the 4.9% forecast and who pays: UK mortgage holders on variable rates, while the BoE catches up with the Fed and ECB. Make the exact vote split clear (the sources differ: 'unanimous' vs 8-1).

stories.label: Another violating oil tanker catches fire in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: New since the four tankers reported ablaze yesterday: another tanker struck a mine east of the Strait of Hormuz early today, by Iran's navy's account (attribute Iranian claims to Mehr/Tasnim; MEE and The New Arab are the independent sources). Lead with what a mined 'unsafe area' does to ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and to Brent crude just as markets priced in peace hopes after the US midterms.

stories.label: Attack appears to hit Russia's Ryazan oil refinery, Reuters analysis finds
stories.summary: Ukraine appears to have struck the Ryazan refinery, one of Russia's largest, while Russia says it hit a Ukrainian postal hub and a ship. Lead with the refinery and the mechanism: Kyiv's long-range drone campaign against Russian fuel capacity, and what losing Ryazan's throughput does to Russian fuel supply and exports at a time of high oil prices. Count civilian harm on both sides symmetrically.

stories.label: ADC rejects judgement sacking Mark, Atiku, blames APC
stories.summary: A Federal High Court ruling on Thursday removed David Mark's leadership of the opposition African Democratic Congress and voided Atiku Abubakar's presidential nomination, months before Nigeria's 2027 election. Lead with what it means: the main opposition coalition's candidate knocked out by a court, the ADC accusing the ruling APC of using the judiciary, and an earlier contradicting ruling recognising Mark. The mechanism is courts as the arena where Nigerian opposition parties are dismantled.

stories.label: PTI workers detained in UAE: LHC terms foreign ministry's report unsatisfactory
stories.summary: Two Pakistanis affiliated with Imran Khan's PTI are held in the UAE, and the Lahore High Court has rejected the foreign ministry's account of what it has done for them, summoning the official responsible. Lead with the accountability gap: a state that will not press a Gulf ally over citizens detained, apparently for their politics, and the diaspora as the new front of Pakistan's crackdown on PTI.

stories.label: Mubadala Energy to double output over next decade with natural gas in focus | The National
stories.summary: Abu Dhabi's Mubadala Energy plans to double output within a decade with gas about 70% of it, and has bought 15% of Egypt's Nargis offshore area next to its Zohr and Nour stakes. Lead with the strategy: a Gulf sovereign fund betting on gas in Egypt, Malaysia and Indonesia while Hormuz is mined, and what it says about Gulf producers building supply outside the strait. Natural gas is a series we chart.

stories.label: Ukraine's central bank opposes crypto bill, citing monetary sovereignty concerns
stories.summary: The National Bank of Ukraine refused to back a bill legalising crypto, warning it threatens monetary sovereignty and leaves the number of trading platforms to the securities regulator's discretion, inviting monopoly and corruption. Lead with the corruption mechanism, in a country whose EU accession is being slowed by graft, and a wartime central bank defending control of its currency against a parallel dollar-stablecoin economy.

stories.label: Chainalysis warns all users hit in cyber breach involving ‘agentic’ techniques
stories.summary: Chainalysis, the blockchain-tracing firm whose customers include police and national security agencies, says information on all its users was exposed in an attack using 'agentic' AI techniques. Lead with who is exposed: the investigators who trace crypto, now themselves identifiable, and the first major breach a company attributes to AI agents. Do not overstate what was taken beyond what Chainalysis disclosed.

stories.label: Staatliche Transparenz: Innenminister will Informationsfreiheit durch die Hintertür einschränken
stories.summary: After FragDenStaat handed more than 680,000 signatures against curbing Germany's freedom of information law to the SPD, the interior ministry is trying to cut the state's duty to disclose by burying it in a critical-infrastructure (KRITIS) bill. Lead with the back-door mechanism: security legislation used to shrink transparency, and what it means for journalists who use FOI to hold Berlin to account.

stories.label: 前华为盘古负责人王云鹤，创业做RSI，掏出1250亿参数智能体大模型
stories.summary: Wang Yunhe, former head of Huawei's Noah's Ark Lab and its Pangu model, now runs Beijing startup TokenRhythm, which released NeoHorse-1.5-Flash (125B total, 6B active parameters) built on Alibaba's Qwen3.8-Flash and trained by 'recursive self-improvement' on records of many models doing the same agent tasks. Lead with the method: a model-routing business that turns other labs' outputs into training data; its Agents' Last Exam score rose 41.2 to 50.4 but maths fell 11%. All results are the company's own.

stories.label: 面壁智能姚远：两年GPT-6级AI跑在手机上，现在点外卖订机票有点无聊
stories.summary: Beijing's ModelBest says its open MiniCPM-V 4.7, a 35B-parameter mixture-of-experts model, now runs on a phone at over 30 tokens a second in about 3GB of memory, by predicting which experts the next layer needs and streaming their weights from flash ahead of time (~80% hit rate). Lead with the mechanism and the privacy stake: frontier-class multimodal AI moving off the cloud and onto the device. Its scientist's claim of GPT-6-level AI on phones within two years is a prediction, and the power draw (like a big mobile game) is the catch.

stories.label: Joshua Wong, face of Hong Kong's pro-democracy movement, sentenced to another 10 years in jail
stories.summary: Already jailed, Joshua Wong got 10 more years under the national security law for conspiring with Nathan Law and others to lobby Western governments for sanctions after 2019. The mechanism: asking foreign states for sanctions is now itself a 'collusion' crime, so advocacy abroad is prosecuted as a security offence. Lead with the sentence length and what he admitted; note Nathan Law remains abroad with a bounty.

stories.label: South Korea to deploy military mission to keep Strait of Hormuz open
stories.summary: Seoul will stretch its Cheonghae anti-piracy unit from Somalia to waters off Duqm, Oman, under US pressure to back the war on Iran. The mechanism: an existing anti-piracy mandate is repurposed so no new parliamentary war vote is needed, while South Korea imports most of its crude through the strait. Tie it to ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, where tankers have been hit by mines this week.

stories.label: How Online Maps Lay Bare the US Military Bases Targeted by Iran
stories.summary: Bellingcat shows that public online maps and imagery reveal the damage Iranian strikes did to US bases across the Gulf, damage the Pentagon has said little about. The accountability angle: open-source evidence against official silence on what eight months of war has cost, and which host states (Qatar, Bahrain, UAE, Iraq) carry the risk. Lead with the specific bases and what the maps show.

stories.label: Nigerian Law School denies barring hijab-wearing candidates from Bar exams
stories.summary: Muslim women say they were harassed or kept out of Bar Final Examination halls on 31 October for wearing the hijab; the Law School denies it and explains why one candidate was stopped. The structural story: Nigeria's legal profession has fought over the hijab since Amasa Firdaus was refused a call to the Bar in 2017, despite court rulings for the right. Report both the allegation and the denial; name who controls access.

stories.label: France braces for fresh protests as unions strike over higher wages
stories.summary: Five unions join a national day of strikes for higher wages, widening protests that began in September with high-school students over school conditions. The economic squeeze: wages lag euro-area inflation near 4%, while a government with no fiscal room faces rising odds of a credit downgrade (Polymarket's France-downgrade market rose from 33% to 49% in a week). Lead with the scale of the turnout and who is striking.

stories.label: Punjab sets wheat sowing target
stories.summary: Punjab set a 16.5-million-acre wheat target and a support price of Rs4,500 per maund for the coming season. The decision matters because Pakistan's growers lost money in past seasons when the state stopped buying wheat, and diesel and fertiliser costs have risen with the Iran war. Tie it to the global wheat price and ask whether the support price covers farmers' costs.

stories.label: In China, a flood of controversial clinical trials slows to a trickle
stories.summary: China's investigator-initiated trials, a fast route that let hospitals test experimental gene and cell therapies in people, have nearly stopped after regulators tightened approvals. Rare-disease families who relied on them, like a Shanghai mother whose 13-year-old daughter is wasting away, are left waiting. The trade-off to explain: speed that drew global biotech to China against the safety lapses that prompted the crackdown.

stories.label: Fractal patterns reveal hidden limits to AI predictability
stories.summary: University of Sydney researchers found a mathematical reason why AI models trained under near-identical conditions learn different behaviours: the boundary between training outcomes is fractal, so tiny changes in settings flip the result. The finding means some AI unreliability cannot be engineered away by tuning alone. Datelined Sydney.

stories.label: Baidu Tests a New Way to Train Robotaxis
stories.summary: Baidu's Apollo unit unveiled Apollo World in Shenzhen, a world model that simulates traffic that reacts to the car, so robotaxis can be trained on generated scenarios instead of only miles driven. Explain the two requirements Baidu sets, causality and interactivity, and why simulation is the race Chinese robotaxi firms are now running.

stories.label: 锁定1276亿大单！谷歌出手担保，Anthropic算力提供方的巨型数据中心开建
stories.summary: Google signed credit-support agreements so that, if Anthropic defaults on its 20-year, ~$19 billion lease of 401 MW at TeraWulf's Justified data center, Google pays the rent or takes over the lease. The mechanism: a former bitcoin miner that lost $941 million last quarter borrows against Google's balance sheet, and Google, an Anthropic investor, gains a likely buyer for its TPUs. Lead with who carries the risk if the AI boom stalls.

stories.label: 海外收入占比据报达50%，Seedance争夺AI视频的商业入口 ｜出海参考
stories.summary: ByteDance's Seedance video model reportedly earns about half its revenue outside China, making it one of the first Chinese AI products to earn most of its money abroad. The Chinese-press view: the test is whether studios and advertisers put it in their production budgets. Explain how it is sold abroad and against whom (Veo, Sora, Kling).

stories.label: Israel's Herzog accepts vote results, opens talks on forming a government
stories.summary: New development since our 2 Nov piece on Eisenkot's 67-seat bloc: Herzog has now accepted the certified results and formally opened consultations, and Netanyahu answered by claiming that letting Arab parties into government would 'dismantle' Israel. Lead with that line — the incumbent's case against the new majority is that one in five citizens cannot share power — and explain how the consultations decide who gets the mandate.

stories.label: Trump: Iran War Will End 'Whenever I Want It To'
stories.summary: In his first press conference since Democrats took both chambers on an anti-war vote, Trump said the Iran war ends 'whenever I want it to' — a claim of sole authority over a war Congress never declared. The mechanism to explain: what a Democratic House and Senate can actually do from January (War Powers resolutions, appropriations) and why the veto still limits them. Iranians and Gulf shipping bear the cost of that timing.

stories.label: Germany's Free Voters party chief found dead in Berlin hotel
stories.summary: Hubert Aiwanger, 55, Bavaria's deputy premier and leader of the Free Voters, was found dead in a Berlin hotel and police and prosecutors have opened an investigation; the cause is unknown. Report only what police say, and explain the political stakes: the Free Voters are the CSU's coalition partner in Bavaria, so his death leaves Germany's largest state government without one of its two leaders.

stories.label: Colombia’s rebels no longer considered political actors under landmark new law
stories.summary: A new Colombian law strips armed groups of political-actor status, ending the legal basis on which the state negotiated with insurgents for six decades — from the FARC accord to 'total peace'. Lead with what that closes: no more political amnesty or peace-table status, so groups like the ELN are treated as criminal organisations. Explain who gains (the security forces) and who bears the risk (rural communities in conflict zones).

stories.label: India expands crude imports with UAE emerging as a major supplier | The National
stories.summary: With ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz disrupted, India now buys crude from about 43 countries and the UAE has become a major supplier. Its oil secretary says he worries more about volatility than about the price level. Lead with the 43 countries: the world's third-largest importer has rebuilt its supply chain around the war. Name Brent crude and ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz as the series.

stories.label: PBOC extends digital yuan to overseas lenders to deepen cross-border flows
stories.summary: The PBOC's upgraded CBETS platform lets overseas banks, Hong Kong branches included, settle digital-yuan payments around the clock without rebuilding their IT systems, and Chinese banks are trying out local e-CNY wallets for foreign firms. Unlike our recent pieces on yuan bonds and the Oman payment link, this is the central bank's own rail going offshore. The mechanism: settlement that bypasses SWIFT and correspondent banking in dollars. Name the yuan as the series.

stories.label: Taunsa farmers hit hard by closure of Chashma Canal
stories.summary: The Chashma Right Bank Canal's Punjab stretch is shut and farmers around Taunsa and Dera Ghazi Khan are losing the sowing season, which they put down to years of skipped maintenance and water theft upstream. Neither the provincial nor the federal government has answered them. Lead with the farmers' losses, then show the mechanism: in Pakistan's canal-fed agriculture, a failure of upkeep becomes a failure of livelihoods.

stories.label: Centuries-old cemetery helps scientists link climate shocks to Industrial Revolution disease
stories.summary: Skeletons from an English cemetery tie the rickets that was common among children during the Industrial Revolution to climate shocks, not only to smog, poverty and latitude, the causes usually given. Lead with the overlooked variable: years of bad weather cut the sunlight and the harvests that growing bones depend on. Today's lesson is that climate stress shows up first in poor children's bodies.

stories.label: 刚刚，Claude Code产品一姐加入OpenAI！
stories.summary: Cat Wu, who led product for Claude Code and Cowork, is leaving Anthropic for OpenAI, where she will run core product. She is the fourth senior Claude Code figure to go since June, and she leaves days after Anthropic filed for an IPO reportedly set for Nasdaq the week of 16 November. Lead with that timing. The structural point is that at AI labs the product lead is now a scarce asset, and losing one can move how an IPO is judged.

stories.label: NASA Announces X-70 “Fractal” Experimental Aircraft
stories.summary: NASA has named a new X-plane, the X-70 'Fractal', to test flight-control technology at the edges of manoeuvrability. Lead with what the aircraft is for — the control problem it is built to solve — and say plainly who uses research like this: control laws proven on X-planes have a history of ending up in military aircraft.

stories.label: Israel's 11-Day Escalated Assault on Hebron
stories.summary: The tally after eleven days of Israel's escalated operation in Hebron: thousands of Palestinians forcibly displaced, families pushed from their homes in the Old City and around the Ibrahimi Mosque. Lead with the number displaced and who ordered the operation; this continues our 10-23 to 10-28 Hebron coverage (lockdown, 407 families displaced, mosque closed), and the new fact is the operation's full extent now it has run eleven days. Name the units and officials; name the displaced.

stories.label: AIPAC dumped more than $55 million into losing midterm races
stories.summary: Two-thirds of AIPAC's $84.1 million midterm spending ($55.3 million) went to races its candidate lost, against 69% wins in 2022 and 87% in 2024; $31.5 million alone failed to stop Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan. Pair it with the material new development: Vice President Vance wrote on X that 'the reason we lost is the war', citing a pollster whose Trump-to-Democrat switchers named ending the war, cost of living and changing the relationship with Israel. The mechanism: the Iran war and unconditional Israel support turned from a fundraising asset into an electoral liability. Spending figures are FEC-reported and Vance's words are public; attribute both.

stories.label: Meet the power brokers in South Africa's great coalition scramble
stories.summary: Results of South Africa's local elections project about 110 hung councils, so more than 100 municipalities, including the metros the DA campaigned to lead, will be run by coalitions negotiated by a handful of party leaders. Lead with the 110 figure and the metros at stake (Johannesburg, Tshwane, Nelson Mandela Bay); the mechanism is that without majorities in local government, water, power and municipal budgets are decided in coalition deals. Follows our 11-01 pre-election story.

stories.label: Los mesones del Centro Histórico: El desalojo silencioso
stories.summary: The government's renewal of San Salvador's Historic Centre is quietly displacing the people who have lived and worked in its mesones, the old shared tenement houses. Lead with who is being moved out and by what mechanism, as Focos documents it, and who gains from the land. A Latin America dateline the audit says we are short of, and a displacement story where the state is the actor.

stories.label: Pakistan Joins Air-to-Air Missile Club With Successful Test Of Fa’az
stories.summary: Pakistan test-fired the Fa'az, its first homegrown air-to-air missile, joining a small club of states that build their own while already fielding advanced Chinese weapons. The structural why: Islamabad is reducing its dependence on a single foreign supplier; give the regional air-power context from the source. Lead with the test and which aircraft carried it; name what is still unproven. No Pakistani outlet in the feed carries it.

stories.label: Coalition threatens mass action over Lagos govt's planned crackdown regarding unlicensed borehole
stories.summary: Lagos plans to seal residential boreholes and prosecute residents who draw groundwater without authorisation, in a megacity where many households rely on their own wells (give the public utility's coverage from the source if it has it). Civil society groups and unions under Our Water Our Right Africa threaten mass action. Lead with who pays: residents the state does not pipe water to are to be penalised for the water they found themselves.

stories.label: US sanctions Indian companies over alleged maritime fraud aiding Iranian vessels
stories.summary: The US Treasury sanctioned what it calls a 'vast criminal network' run by two Indian nationals that helped Iran's shadow fleet of oil tankers sail under fraudulent flags. Lead with the mechanism (false flag registrations, ship identities) and the Indian firms named; the why is that Iran's wartime oil exports run through third-country paperwork, and Washington is now targeting the service providers, not only the tankers. Name Brent crude in context: the shadow fleet is how sanctioned barrels still reach market.

stories.label: Wall Street Is Helping China Build a Global Yuan
stories.summary: Wall Street firms are now tapping Hong Kong's offshore yuan 'dim sum' bond market, while Beijing curbs the yuan's rise as China heads for a record trade surplus (SCMP). The new fact against our 11-02/11-03 PBOC stories: US finance itself is deepening the yuan's offshore market. Report the issuance facts, not the column's opinion; name the yuan and the mechanism (cheap yuan funding against dollar rates).

stories.label: Pharma critic Bernie Sanders is set to hold major sway over FDA funding bill
stories.summary: The Democratic Senate gives Bernie Sanders major sway over PDUFA, the law under which drugmakers' user fees fund much of the FDA's drug-review staff, just as it comes up for reauthorisation. The mechanism to explain: industry pays for its own reviews, so the must-pass bill is leverage, and Sanders can use it to press FDA and drug-industry reforms. Lead with the size of the fee stream and what Sanders has said he wants.

stories.label: More Asian airlines announce data breaches after attack on Spanish IT provider Amadeus
stories.summary: Japan Airlines, Cathay Pacific, Korean Air, Asiana, Singapore Airlines and Malaysia Airlines have each disclosed passenger data breaches in the past week, all traced to one supplier: Amadeus, which runs reservation, ticketing and check-in platforms for much of the industry. Lead with six carriers and one root; the structural point is single-vendor concentration, where one compromise exposes travellers across a continent.

stories.label: London, Paris, Berlin: Action Against Data Centers Goes Europe-Wide This Weekend
stories.summary: The 'Stop Dirty Data Centres' coalition calls for an immediate moratorium on large data centres in Europe, with protests and community actions on 6-7 November in London, Paris and Berlin, including against a planned site in south Berlin. The angle: a day after US voters rejected AI data centres at the ballot, the backlash is organised across Europe. Lead with the moratorium demand and the water and power such sites draw; keep the US vote to one line of context.

stories.label: AI is forcing us to pay off 40 years of technical debt
stories.summary: IEEE Spectrum on the PHP2Shell vulnerability: AI tools now surface decades-old flaws in legacy code faster than maintainers can patch them, so the security debt of 40 years of software is coming due at once. Lead with the specific flaw and how it was found; the reader is a developer who maintains old code. 959 points on Hacker News.

stories.label: 高通连续九年全勤赴约进博会，6G终端原型机将迎全球首展
stories.summary: At Shanghai's import expo Qualcomm shows in public, for the first time, a 6G terminal prototype built to 3GPP's latest definition, already used in interoperability tests with China Mobile and ZTE (400 MHz bandwidth, about 14 Gbps peak). The angle: amid US-China tech rivalry, the US chip firm is building 6G alongside Chinese carriers and vendors, aiming at commercial 6G from 2029, before the first 6G standard (Release 21) is final. Report it as the Chinese tech press does.

stories.label: Ukraine falls behind Moldova on path to EU membership
stories.summary: Kyiv and Chisinau applied together, but the European Commission's enlargement report now proposes different end dates for their membership talks, and blames Ukraine's sputtering anti-corruption effort. Lead with the decoupling: a country at war is told its courts and graft bodies, not the front line, set its pace. Add the wider Balkan picture (Montenegro praised, stagnation elsewhere) from Balkan Insight.

stories.label: Election stiffens the Fed's guardrails, but independence risks remain
stories.summary: A Democratic Senate takes the confirmation gate for Fed governors away from Trump: the Banking Committee (with Elizabeth Warren's camp ascendant) can now block nominees picked to push rates down. Lead with the mechanism — appointments, not speeches, are how a president bends a central bank — and what remains exposed before January. Name the Fed funds rate and the US 10-year Treasury yield.

stories.label: Eurozone inflation rises to 4% in October
stories.summary: Eurozone inflation reached 4% in October, driven by fossil-fuel prices from the Iran war, while the Bank of England's new 'sticky' gauge shows UK pressures not yet building ahead of its meeting this week. Lead with the divergence: energy shock feeds through to the euro area first, which puts the ECB rate and a December hike (floated by the Bundesbank's Nagel) on the table. Name the ECB rate and the euro.

stories.label: Oil prices tumble below $100 on post-election peace hopes
stories.summary: Brent crude fell below $100 to a two-month low as traders priced the Democratic landslide as pressure on Trump to end the Iran war; JD Vance blamed the defeat on anger over the war. Lead with the mechanism: a vote in Washington moved the war-risk premium on Gulf barrels, a day after tankers burned in Hormuz. Name Brent crude, WTI and ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz; note that importers like Pakistan cut pump prices the same day.

stories.label: American Voters Overwhelmingly Reject AI Data Centers
stories.summary: Data centers were on the ballot in dozens of local measures and races, and lost most of them; in Texas, governor-elect Gina Hinojosa ousted Greg Abbott pledging to crack down on server-warehouse growth. Lead with the count of measures lost, then the mechanism: power bills, water and grid connections turned AI infrastructure into a local voting issue. Consequence: Wall Street cut targets for bitcoin miners and data-center builders, while miners already holding approved power connections may gain.

stories.label: French blood banks targeted by refrigerator cyberattack
stories.summary: Attackers tried to destroy stored blood plasma by driving cold-storage temperatures past boiling, in a wave of attacks on refrigeration control systems across several European countries on Sunday and Monday, French authorities said. Lead with the target: not data but physical medical stock, through the internet-connected controllers that run cold chains. Who is exposed (hospitals, supermarkets) and who is suspected.

stories.label: War, drought, inflation: How Sudan is edging closer to famine
stories.summary: Poor seasonal harvests and runaway inflation are compounding three years of SAF-RSF war, pushing millions of Sudanese toward famine. Lead with the convergence: war cut planting, drought cut yields, and the collapsing pound priced what remains out of reach. Name who blocks access and who holds the routes; continuation of the siege is the development.

stories.label: Opposition leaders gather at JUI-F chief Fazl's Islamabad residence to discuss KP emergency
stories.summary: Pakistan's opposition, PTI included, convened at Maulana Fazlur Rehman's residence over the imposition of an emergency and governor's rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, the province PTI governs. Lead with the power move: Islamabad suspending an elected provincial government, and the constitutional mechanism used. Who loses representation, and whether the opposition alliance can contest it.

stories.label: Inflación, sequía y alza de costos de producción presionan los precios de los alimentos y las familias hondureñas recortan sus compras
stories.summary: Fuel costs from the Iran war, an El Niño drought and rising production costs are pushing food prices up in Honduras: inflation hit 6.28% in September and 1.8 million Hondurans face crisis or emergency food insecurity. Lead with the market-stall view — families cutting and substituting — then the chain from a war in the Gulf to a Tegucigalpa farmers' fair.

stories.label: Q&A: What is in the global ‘roadmap’ for transitioning away from fossil fuels?
stories.summary: Brazil's COP30 presidency has released a first-of-its-kind global roadmap for transitioning away from fossil fuels, alongside a separate roadmap to end deforestation. Lead with what it actually asks of producers and who signed on, and what it lacks: no binding dates. The angle for this reader: Gulf petrostates and Indonesia's forests are the two places it bites. Filed as politics: a policy document, not a finding.

stories.label: NASA's Swift Observatory Is Crashing Back to Earth Today After 21 Years in Orbit
stories.summary: NASA's Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory, the 3,200-pound gamma-ray-burst hunter, re-enters the atmosphere after 21 years. Lead with what science loses: Swift's rapid slewing found and localised thousands of gamma-ray bursts and fed follow-up of gravitational-wave events, and no replacement with that response time is flying. Note the orbit decayed under high solar activity. Keep it factual and cite NASA's own figures, not the outlet's framing.

stories.label: Hermes Agent手机端要来了！能读取手机数据，内测名额秒没
stories.summary: Nous Research's open-source Hermes Agent opened a mobile beta whose 'Device Access' feature lets agents read the phone's calendar, contacts, location and health data — sent on to the user's server and the AI provider behind it. Lead with that data flow, then the pricing ($0.60-2.50 a day for cloud-hosted agents) and the race with OpenClaw's poorly received app. Reported from China's developer community by Zhidx.

stories.label: Ukrainian news outlet Kyiv Independent hit by suspected Russian cyberattack
stories.summary: A suspected Russian cyberattack took down the website of The Kyiv Independent, one of Ukraine's main English-language outlets — days after a destructive attack on Russian host Beget. Lead with the target: the outlet foreign readers rely on for the war, hit as US-mediated talks approach in Abu Dhabi. Attack type, duration and attribution evidence.

stories.label: Elon Musk's $500 Million Bet Fails to Help Republicans
stories.summary: The world's richest man spent nearly $500 million on Republican candidates, a record for one donor, and the candidates he backed lost, Ken Paxton's Texas Senate race (the most expensive in US history) among them. Lead with what that money bought: almost nothing. The mechanism: unlimited super PAC spending after Citizens United lets one fortune buy airtime but not votes when the war and fuel prices are driving them. Al Jazeera notes Musk made light of the defeats. Do not repeat the overall results already covered; this is the story of money in politics.

stories.label: Firsts for women and minorities in US midterm elections
stories.summary: New since our 3 November story on the Islamophobic closing pitch in Michigan: Abdul El-Sayed won the Senate seat, about 52% to 46%, and becomes the first Muslim US senator, after AIPAC-linked super PACs spent a record $30.6 million against him in the primary and at least $12.7 million in the general. Lead with El-Sayed and that spending; then list the other firsts for women and minorities. Dateline Michigan.

stories.label: Iran supreme leader says those expecting US policy shift 'seriously mistaken'
stories.summary: Hours after the Democratic sweep, Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei told Iranians not to expect any change in US behaviour, while adviser Mohammad Mokhber claimed Iran had won by shifting the war's costs onto the United States and spokesman Baghaei said Iran would not be intimidated. Lead with Tehran's line: the vote changes nothing. The mechanism: a Democratic Congress can cut war funding when government funding runs out on 11 December, but the war powers stay with Trump until January. Attribute the Mehr quotes to Iranian state media. Tie it to the Doha talks and to the five conditions Tehran set this week.

stories.label: Короли асфальта. С кем связаны фирмы, «провалившие» ремонт дорог в Бишкеке?
stories.summary: Kloop's investigation: Bishkek spent at least 740 million som rebuilding the Auezov Street bridge and parts of Baitik Baatyr and Akhunbaev streets, and the new asphalt sagged and slid within months. Two of the three contractors are tied to former and current officials, and the city ignores complaints. Lead with the money and the tie to officials. The mechanism is procurement capture: officials award public works to firms they are connected to, and no one answers for the failure. Kyrgyzstan dateline.

stories.label: Segurança Pública: PEC da redução da maioridade penal no Senado pode ter relator do PT
stories.summary: Brazil's Senate has passed the Public Security constitutional amendment, and a second amendment lowering the age of criminal responsibility may be taken up on Wednesday, possibly with a rapporteur from Lula's own PT. Lead with who would be affected: teenagers, overwhelmingly Black and poor, moved into an adult prison system already over capacity. The mechanism: a tough-on-crime push before the 2026 vote, and a governing party weighing whether to steer the amendment or resist it. Brazil dateline.

stories.label: Tinubu's ADC seeks arrest of Kwara lawyer over alleged land grabbing
stories.summary: President Tinubu's aide-de-camp, Lt-Col Nurudeen Yusuf, who is also a traditional ruler in Kwara State, has started criminal defamation proceedings against lawyer Nuruddin Abdulsalam and is seeking his arrest, after Abdulsalam accused him of land grabbing and abuse of power. Lead with the inversion: the man accused of taking land is the one asking police to arrest his accuser. The mechanism: criminal defamation, which press-freedom groups have long asked Nigeria to repeal, still lets officials put critics in jail. Kwara, Nigeria dateline.

stories.label: Democratic sweep adds new twist to markets' Iran, AI, and debt worries
stories.summary: Reuters from London: a divided Washington is the newest problem for markets already dealing with the Iran war's oil shock, an AI boom pushing up growth and inflation, and the US debt load. Gold jumped about 3% to above $4,060 an ounce on Comex (TASS figures). Lead with gold and the US 10-year Treasury yield, and say why: gridlock over spending and the debt ceiling against a war-driven inflation risk. Do not repeat the dollar/yen move already covered. Dateline London.

stories.label: Bitcoin briefly sinks to $75,700 as bets on a Democratic sweep rattle markets
stories.summary: Bitcoin fell to about $75,700 as the returns came in, because Democrats oppose the CLARITY Act, the crypto industry's market-structure bill, and a Democratic Congress can now stall it and question stablecoin policy. The industry spent heavily for a friendly Congress and lost. Lead with the bill, not the price; chart bitcoin. Merge CoinDesk's analyst roundup on the blue Congress for what changes for stablecoins.

stories.label: Tokenization news: $1.1T Schroders brings emerging market bond fund to Solana
stories.summary: Schroders, a 200-year-old London manager with $1.1 trillion under management, is putting an emerging-market bond fund on the public Solana blockchain. That takes Wall Street's tokenization push from money-market funds into the debt of developing countries. Lead with what it changes: holders of Global South sovereign and corporate debt could trade around the clock on a public chain, and who carries the custody and settlement risk is still untested. London dateline.

stories.label: Smiling can make you happier—unless someone forces you to do it
stories.summary: Nicholas Coles, whose own research was cited as evidence that forcing a smile lifts your mood, tested that result again and found the effect disappears when people are told to smile. Lead with a scientist checking and narrowing his own famous finding. This is the replication crisis in psychology working as it should, and it bears on every self-help and wellness claim built on the original result.

stories.label: 英伟达团队下场！国产视频模型开源，硅谷公司上门谈授权
stories.summary: An Nvidia team and the US video start-up Pika are both building on MiniMax's open-weight Chinese video model H3, which has passed 24 million downloads and 300 derivative models, and Nvidia's project involves a commercial licence from MiniMax. The surprise is in the licence: the free community licence excludes the US, the EU, the UK and South Korea, so Western firms have to negotiate with a Chinese lab, and any user earning over $20 million a year needs written permission. Lead with the reversal: Silicon Valley building on Chinese open weights. China dateline.

stories.label: Cyberattack wipes cloud data at major Russian hosting provider Beget
stories.summary: A cyberattack destroyed data across the cloud infrastructure of Beget, one of Russia's largest hosting providers, and hundreds of websites are down while it tries to restore them. Lead with the wiper: this was destruction, not ransom. Say who has claimed it, if anyone, and where it fits in the cyber front of the Ukraine war, where hitting one shared host takes out thousands of businesses at once. Russia dateline.

stories.label: Bezahlkarte für Asylsuchende: Berlin setzt Bargeld-Obergrenze aus
stories.summary: Berlin has suspended the cash withdrawal cap on the payment card asylum seekers must use, which limited how much of their own benefit they could take out in cash in a city where many shops and services do not take cards. The Berlin Refugee Council calls it a partial victory. Lead with how the card works: a payment system designed to control what refugees can spend. Whether the card is scrapped altogether now depends on Berlin's coalition talks. Berlin dateline.
